title: Unique Games Conjecture
statement: For every real $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, there is a positive natural number $q$ such that the promise problem whose yes instances are unique games with alphabet size $q$ and optimum at least $1-\varepsilon$, and whose no instances are unique games with alphabet size $q$ and optimum less than $\varepsilon$, is promise NP-hard.
hypotheses_covered: For every real $\varepsilon$ in the open interval $(0,1/2)$
There exists a natural number $q$ with $0<q$
The stated yes/no promise problem is promise NP-hard
